req.title: Reject negative squadNumber
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when squadNumber is not a positive integer.

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-023 requires HTTP 422 when squadNumber is not a positive integer. The PlayerRequestModel defines squad_number as int with no explicit validator, so Pydantic must enforce positivity. We need: (1) a positive test confirming a valid positive squadNumber is accepted (HTTP 201), (2) a negative test confirming a negative squadNumber is rejected (HTTP 422), and (3) boundary tests at squadNumber=0 (not positive, should be 422), squadNumber=1 (minimum positive, should be 201), and squadNumber=-1 (one below zero boundary, should be 422). We also test squadNumber=-999 as a deep-negative EP case. All tests use FastAPI TestClient in-process. Mutation resilience: exact status code assertions (422 vs 201), boundary ±1 around zero, both sides of the positive-integer threshold.

tests.name: test_post_player_valid_positive_squad_number_returns_201
preconditions: Database contains pre-loaded rows with squadNumbers 1-26
squadNumber 99 does not exist in the database
actions: POST /players/ with a valid payload where squadNumber=99 (a positive integer not in the DB)
expected: Response body contains firstName matching the submitted value
trace: R-PLAYER-023: positive integer squadNumber must be accepted
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_post_player_valid_positive_squad_number_returns_201():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Test",
        "lastName": "Player",
        "squadNumber": 99,
        "position": "Goalkeeper"
    }
    r = client.post("/players/", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    body = r.json()
    assert body["squadNumber"] == 99
    assert body["firstName"] == "Test"
    assert body["lastName"] == "Player"
    assert body["position"] == "Goalkeeper"
    assert "id" in body

test_post_player_valid_positive_squad_number_returns_201()

tests.name: test_post_player_squad_number_one_returns_201

actions: POST /players/ with squadNumber=1 (minimum positive integer boundary)
Expect HTTP 409 because squadNumber=1 already exists, confirming the request passed validation (not 422)
expected: HTTP 409 Conflict (not 422) — validation passed, conflict detected
trace: R-PLAYER-023: squadNumber=1 is the minimum positive integer; must pass validation (not 422)
BVA: one is the minimum valid positive integer boundary; a 409 proves validation succeeded

from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_post_player_squad_number_one_returns_not_422():
    # squadNumber=1 already exists in the DB, so we expect 409 (conflict),

    payload = {
        "firstName": "Anjali",
        "lastName": "Banerjee",
        "squadNumber": 1,
        "position": "Defensive Midfield"
    }
    r = client.post("/players/", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 409
    assert r.status_code != 422
    assert r.status_code != 201
